description: RailSystemModel, formerly RailTopoModel, is the UIC's generalist, functional, project-independent and implementable model of the railway system, giving a universal representation of a railway network and associated events as a structural backbone for digital railway data. RailTopoModel 1.0 was released as International Railway Solution IRS 30100 in April 2016 and maintenance release 1.1 followed on 10 November 2017; the scope was later extended and the model renamed, with version 1.2 documented on its own site. Coverage: concepts across track, signalling, energy, telecom, rolling stock, capacity planning, traffic management and civil works planning, and across functional, spatial, topology, geometry, time and lifecycle, and observation dimensions; it cooperates with expert models such as Eulynx for signalling, IFC Rail for BIM and ERA RINF, and railML 3 is built on it. The 1.1 release provides class diagrams per package (common, location, net entity, network, topology), revision notes and a list of changes. Format and access: PDF class diagrams and a zip archive on the UIC page, and HTML documentation of RSM 1.2 on rsm.uic.org; free for research, commercial and operational use. Licence: the RSM site states that all information is licensed under EUPL 1.2. Caveats: rsm.uic.org showed injected gambling spam links in its page text on 28 September 2026, so the site appears compromised and should be treated with care; the version 1.2 documentation is rendered by scripts and was not read. Simulation uses: a common topology model for rail network graphs used in capacity, disruption and asset models. Related records: railML (data-railml) implements the model, and ERA's register of infrastructure (data-era-rinf) is a linked domain view.
